adminGuide.title: Site operations guide
adminGuide.intro: Common settings and workflows that guild operators often miss. Each section links directly to where you can edit it.

quickStart.title: First-time setup — 7-step checklist
quickStart.intro: Just installed the bot? Walk through these 7 steps in order before launching. Skipping any of them tends to break other features later.
quickStart.step1: Discord bot install — happens automatically when you sign up. If the bot is missing or under-permissioned, re-invite from albion-guildmanager.com/invite.
quickStart.step2: Set the Albion home guild — Settings → Guild tab, search for your guild name, and link it. This anchors verification, killboard, and stats, so do this first.
quickStart.step3: Pick the operating timezone — same screen. Choose KR (KST) / EU (CET·CEST) / NA (EST·EDT) / SA (BRT) based on where most of your members live.
quickStart.step4: Configure admin roles — Settings → Permissions tab. Pick at least one Discord role that should grant admin access. Confirm one of your own roles is in the list.
quickStart.step5: Wire up the notification channel and role — Settings → Events tab. Choose the Discord channel where events get posted and the role to mention. Without this, the channel-announce button silently fails.
quickStart.step6: Run a tiny test event — create a small dry-run event and walk through publish → notify → bulk-payout once. Future operations go smoothly after this rehearsal.
quickStart.step7: Invite your members — share the site URL (or albion-guildmanager.com/invite) and ask new members to verify their Albion nickname through the onboarding modal.

roleLoops.title: Role-based operating loops
roleLoops.intro: Each officer should operate from their own work area. Do not place large task blocks inside member-facing pages; keep summaries in the top status chip and approval badges.
roleLoops.eventLead: Event lead: finish recruiting, party edits, announcements, and bulk rewards from Event admin, then open supply or finance pages only when needed.
roleLoops.regearOfficer: Regear officer: mainly watch the Regear tab in Approvals and regear windows. Exchange and donation reviews require separate finance approval permissions.
roleLoops.financeOfficer: Finance officer: review Exchange / Donation tabs in Approvals and check Stats. Regear price edits or inventory delivery still require separate permissions.
roleLoops.supplyOfficer: Supply officer: run Guild shop, Guild inventory, Loot audit, and Craft regear. Use each feature page's filters and badges for member requests.
roleLoops.analyst: Analyst: review Battles, Stats, and Audit log to support operations. This can stay read-heavy without granting mutation permissions.

eventLifecycle.title: Event lifecycle
eventLifecycle.step1: Create event: fill in time/location/notes. Saved as draft initially.
eventLifecycle.step2: Configure parties/slots: load a template or add parties → set role, gear, and spec per slot.
eventLifecycle.step3: Publish: use the banner button to move the event to a state where members can apply.
eventLifecycle.step4: Mark battle started: press the 'Battle Started' button to lock the battle start time. Regear window timer begins from this moment.
eventLifecycle.step5: After the event: the auto-regear job reads killboard and generates approvals. Members can submit manual regear once the window opens. Use the 'Bulk payout' button at the top of the event page to grant a fixed attendance point to every assigned member in one click.

regear.title: Regear system
regear.body: Three regear modes coexist: auto (killboard-based), event-tied manual (screenshot-based), and 'regear windows' (event-independent open intake). Setting the per-role reward cap to 0 blocks all regear claims from that role.
regear.bullet1: The auto-regear toggle is a global switch. It must be ON for killboard deaths to be converted into approvals automatically.
regear.bullet2: Slot editor has 'Exclude from auto-regear' (visible only when global ON) and 'Exclude from manual regear' (always) checkboxes for per-build opt-out.
regear.bullet3: Event-tied manual regear opens N minutes after battle start. Max screenshot 10MB, PNG/JPEG/WebP only.
regear.bullet4: Auto-generated pending rows let the claimant edit per-slot prices. Admins review at /admin/dashboard/regear.
regear.bullet5: Event-independent free regear is accepted via 'regear windows'. Open and close them at /admin/dashboard/regear-windows (or via the admin-only button on the top right of /regear) — set a title, deadline, and per-user cap. The deadline uses the same 4-part (month/day/hour/minute) input as events for mobile-friendly entry.

craftRegear.title: Crafted regear (guild boxes)
craftRegear.body: Crafted regear is a guild-wide payout mode for new regear claims. Off creates new claims as silver; on creates them as craft candidates. During admin review, officers finish each claim as a silver payout, a craft-queue task, or a stock issue. Crafted payouts then show the requester a pickup box on My craft pickups. Multiple parts for the same requester share the same box.
craftRegear.bullet1: In Admin → Craft regear, grant 'Crafter' permission to selected members. Only crafters can claim queued tasks.
craftRegear.bullet2: Assign each crafter a 'box range' (e.g., 1-10). The server blocks overlapping ranges between crafters automatically. Without a range, auto-assign is disabled and the crafter must enter a number manually.
craftRegear.bullet3: When a crafter opens the Deliver dialog, the system picks a box automatically: (1) reuse the same box if the requester already has one in use, otherwise (2) the smallest free number in the crafter's range. The crafter can override manually.
craftRegear.bullet4: A box only frees up once the requester collects (or it expires). Multiple parts may stack in the same box, so remind requesters to collect everything in a single trip.
craftRegear.bullet5: Per-role caps, the global box-number range (1-999), expiry days, and focus bonus all live in the 'Settings' card at the top. The 'Active tasks' panel below shows every task in flight; admins can force-cancel or convert to silver from there.

onboarding.title: Albion nickname verification
onboarding.body:
New members see an Albion server/nickname onboarding modal after login. On successful verification, both the site and Discord guild nicknames sync to the Albion name.

Verification requires an 'Albion home guild ID' set in Settings → Guild tab. Without it, identities are stored but left unverified (verifiedAt=null).

A single Albion home guild can only belong to one site at a time — if another site has already claimed the same guild, that one must release it before you can verify here. During initial setup, choosing the home guild also auto-syncs the subdomain slug to the guild name. Changing the home guild later does NOT rename the subdomain.

The Stats page shows unverified/pending members. The 'Re-onboard' button clears a member's albion_* fields so the modal shows again.

timezone.title: Operating timezone
timezone.body:
The site-wide reference timezone for displaying and entering all times. During initial setup, pick KR (KST) / EU (CET·CEST) / NA (EST·EDT) / SA (BRT). All gather times, battle starts, regear deadlines, and stats follow this zone.

The same timezone drives auto-regear day boundaries, the 'today/this week' grouping in stats, and the 35-min Discord DM alert. Setting it to where the majority of your members live cuts down on "what time is that?" confusion.

You can change it any time in Settings → Guild tab. Stored absolute timestamps stay the same — only how they're displayed changes.

bombSquad.title: Bomb-squad party & caller
bombSquad.body:
Bomb-squad parties use a 'members apply freely → caller approves/direct-assigns' flow. To use it:

1) Go to Settings → Permissions and configure at least one caller role.
2) Have at least one guild member with that role.
3) In the event party editor, toggle 'Bomb Squad' on and pick a caller.

Callers manage their own party's slots and members directly from a dedicated edit page.

shop.title: Guild shop
shop.body:
Members exchange points they earned for gear. Stock syncs by copying and pasting the Albion log into the import form.

The 'exchange / discount rate' converts silver prices into point prices. 100% means silver price equals point price; 50% sells at half price.

When item prices diverge sharply from current market or look unusual, an automatic warning appears. Review and adjust those rows manually.

siphon.title: Siphon ledger
siphon.body: Paste in-game siphon deposit/withdraw logs to calculate each member's balance. Set the official accounting start on the siphon admin page (or Settings → Guild), and if the ledger gets polluted, reset the raw siphon logs from the same page before importing again.

lootAudit.title: Loot log audit
lootAudit.body: Compare post-ZvZ personal loot CSVs with guild chest deposit logs to find suspected missing returns. The first loot timestamp in each audit becomes the reference point, and only guild chest deposit rows before that time are excluded.

notifications.title: Discord notifications
notifications.body:
Notifications are delivered three ways:

- Channel announcement: posted to the event channel with a role mention. Goes out only when you press the manual button after creating or editing an event.
- Personal DM: auto-sent to assigned members before the event gather time. The lead time follows the guild default (initially 35 min, configurable in the Events tab → Event notifications); each member can override it in 'My settings', or opt out entirely. Approval / rejection of regear or point exchange also triggers a DM to the requester.
- Admin operations alerts: pending approvals, shop orders, craft deliveries, sync delays, and unverified members can be sent to a separate admin-only channel. Configure topics, mention roles, and 30 min / 1 h / 3 h / daily digest intervals.

This requires the Discord bot, notification channels, roles, and permissions to be configured first. After a fresh bot invite, check Settings → Events/Notifications for the channel and role mappings.

battles.title: Battle records (auto-aggregated)
battles.body: Guild-vs-guild ZvZ fights are auto-fetched from the Albion API hourly — no manual entry or screenshots required. Battles appear in the list shortly after they end. Keep these classification rules in mind so you can answer members asking why their fight isn't shown. Full ruleset lives behind the 'Show classification rules' disclosure on the /battles page.
battles.bullet1: Size buckets are based on the main opponent (single alliance or standalone guild) headcount: small 10-30, middle 31-60, large 61-100, zerg 101+.
battles.bullet2: Encounters with fewer than 10 players (ganks, straggler kills) are not ZvZ and are filtered out (10-player cutoff).
battles.bullet3: Low-engagement events (scouting, retreats, failed escapes) where K+D is far below team size are filtered too — the same Albion battle id may exist upstream but won't appear here.
battles.bullet4: A single large battle in which we fight two alliances back-to-back is split into per-opponent rows.

stats.title: Stats & monitoring
stats.body: Top/bottom point holders, event participation, shop/regear activity, and Albion verification status in one page. Use the inline 'Re-onboard' button to restart the onboarding flow for unverified members.

tips.title: Operation tips
tips.tip1: Before making big changes, run through the global toggles on the Settings page (auto-regear, auto-start, etc.) once.
tips.tip2: Save your common party layouts as templates so you can reuse them when building events. Re-saving with the same name prompts whether to overwrite the existing template.
tips.tip3: Use the party editor's 'Hide party' button to hide work-in-progress parties from members.
tips.tip4: If unexplained errors keep happening, first check bot permissions, channel settings, and the home guild setting, then share the details with your site admin.
tips.tip5: Share albion-guildmanager.com/invite as a one-click bot install link with your guild — it lands directly on the Discord bot invite page.
tips.tip6: Event gather time and regear-window deadlines now use the same 4-part (month/day/hour/minute) inputs everywhere, so mobile keypads stay consistent. Times convert to your operating timezone automatically.
tips.tip7: Reminder DMs use a guild-wide default (Settings → Events → Event notifications), and members can override their personal lead time anywhere from 5 to 1440 minutes in /me/settings. Useful when commute schedules differ across the roster.

troubleshooting.title: Troubleshooting
troubleshooting.intro: Common issues and how to fix them. If you're still stuck, check Discord bot permissions and server settings first, then contact your site admin.
troubleshooting.p1Title: A member can't verify their Albion nickname
troubleshooting.p1Body: Make sure the 'Albion home guild' is set in Settings → Guild tab — verification won't complete without it. If another site has already claimed the same Albion guild as its home, that one needs to release it first.
troubleshooting.p2Body: Confirm the home guild and the Albion server (Americas / Europe / Asia) match. The Albion API polls every 5 minutes, so kills from the last 5–10 minutes appear shortly after. Kills from unverified members may also be missing from aggregates.
troubleshooting.p3Body: Check that the global 'auto-regear' toggle is ON in Settings → Regear, the per-slot 'Exclude from auto-regear' is OFF, and the per-role cap isn't 0. Auto-regear only recognizes Black Zone deaths and always creates rows in the 'pending' state — admins must approve before payout.
troubleshooting.p4Body: Channel announcements require the channel and role to be set in Settings → Events, plus a manual 'send announcement' click after publishing. Personal DMs only arrive when the bot is in the same Discord server as the member and the member hasn't disabled notifications in /me/settings.
troubleshooting.p5Title: Battles aren't showing up in records
troubleshooting.p5Body: Encounters with fewer than 10 of our members are filtered as ganks. Low-engagement events (scouting, retreats) where K+D is far below team size are also filtered. The full ruleset is behind 'Show classification rules' on the battles page.
troubleshooting.p6Body: First confirm they're logging in with their own Discord account and are members of a Discord server the bot is in. If they aren't recognized as admin, verify the admin role configured in Settings → Permissions is actually granted to them.
troubleshooting.p7Body: 'Exchange / discount rate' converts silver to points: 100% means silver-equals-points, 50% means half-price. Large divergence from market triggers an automatic warning. Market price refresh can lag, so re-check after a few minutes.

adminShopInventory.title: Stock / price
adminShopInventory.resetTitle: Delete all shop items + raw logs + disable baseline + auto-cancel pending orders
adminShopInventory.descriptionPrefix: Pulls market prices (using admin server/city/mode settings) for the entire stock in one batch. Manual prices take precedence over auto. Points·silver are 1:1, shown after the exchange / discount rate
adminShopInventory.recoveryDescription: Reset and rebuild are recovery tasks, not regular shop operations. They can affect stored raw logs, baselines, and pending orders, so use them only after confirming the ledger is out of sync with the real guild chest.
adminShopInventory.freshStartDescription: Use this when the in-game chest log is tangled or you want to discard the current shop and start again. It clears stored raw logs and current shop stock, then disables the confirmed baseline.
adminShopInventory.freshStartPreserves: Completed orders, blacklist entries, and name overrides are preserved. Pending orders are cancelled automatically.
adminShopInventory.resetSummary: Deleted {rows} item row(s) and {logs} raw log row(s). Disabled {baselines} baseline(s) and auto-cancelled {orders} pending order(s).
adminShopInventory.resetConfirm: This deletes every shop item row and raw chest log. The confirmed baseline is also disabled, so later rebuilds cannot restore the previous snapshot. Stock, manual prices, and auto-price metadata will all be removed, and pending orders will be cancelled automatically. Approved, rejected, and cancelled orders, blacklist entries, and overrides are preserved. Continue?
adminShopInventory.resetAutoCancelNote: Automatically cancelled by shop inventory reset
adminShopInventory.rebuildTitle: Recompute stock from raw chest logs using the operating start time
adminShopInventory.rebuildSummary: Rebuild complete. Total stock {before} → {after}, {changed} changed item(s).
adminShopInventory.rebuildConfirm: This recomputes stock from the stored raw chest logs using the operating start time. If the start time is empty, all logs are used. Manual prices and auto-price metadata for the same item are preserved. Continue?
adminShopInventory.emptyNoInventory: No stock. Start with a log import.
adminShopInventory.stockMustBeNonNegInt: Stock must be a non-negative integer.
adminShopInventory.priceMustBeNonNegInt: Price must be a non-negative integer.
adminShopInventory.priceSourceEmpty: Edit manual price (silver, before exchange / discount rate) · blank = auto
adminShopInventory.priceSourceManualLocked: Manual fixed price (silver, before exchange / discount rate) · save blank to revert to auto
adminShopInventory.priceSourceSpot: No history in the configured average window, falling back to spot quote
adminShopInventory.priceSourceQualityFallback: No market data for the requested quality, falling back to quality {quality} ({label}) — actual price may differ
adminShopInventory.deleteBlockedTitle: Rows with remaining stock cannot be deleted

adminShopOrderReview.saveQuotePriceTitle: Save this member suggestion as the item's manual price
adminShopOrderReview.insufficientBalance: Insufficient balance — cannot approve as-is. Lower the total to approve adjusted.
adminShopOrderReview.insufficientStock: Insufficient stock — restock and retry, or reject.
adminShopOrderReview.adjustTotalTitle: Approve with a custom order total
adminShopOrderReview.adjustTotalPrompt: Enter the point total to charge. Current order total {total}p, applicant balance {balance}p.
adminShopOrderReview.totalMustBePositiveInt: Total must be an integer of 1 or higher.
adminShopOrderReview.adjustInsufficientBalance: The adjusted total cannot exceed the applicant's balance ({amount}p).

adminShopImport.title: Guild chest log sync
adminShopImport.description: Copy the latest section of the in-game guild chest log, then let the site apply only the new confirmed rows to stock. Pasting does not change stock; the public shop updates only after you review the result and apply it.
adminShopImport.syncGuideTitle: How should I paste the log?
adminShopImport.syncGuideStepCopy: 1. Copy the latest section from the in-game guild chest log.
adminShopImport.syncGuideStepCheck: 2. Include a few rows that overlap with the site's last applied log when possible.
adminShopImport.syncGuideStepApply: 3. When the site ignores duplicates and shows only new rows, apply them to stock.
adminShopImport.syncGuideOverlapHint: Overlapping is safe. It helps the site confirm the handoff point and detect missing middle sections.
adminShopImport.checkpointEmpty: No guild chest log has been saved yet. For first-time setup, confirm a current stock baseline first if possible.
adminShopImport.firstImportHint: If this is your first guild chest import, incomplete historical logs can distort inventory. Use "Inventory baseline" first to lock the current chest stock, then accumulate only new logs from that point.
adminShopImport.placeholder:
Paste copied text from the in-game "Bank" log. Example:
"04/21/2026 15:59:10"	"SoonSem"	"Lightning Coil"	"0"	"1"	"-1"
"04/21/2026 13:42:13"	"WarGloves"	"Cleric Robe"	"1"	"2"	"1"
adminShopImport.fileReadFail: Failed to read file — drop a .txt or .rtf file.
adminShopImport.stagingNoPrevBody: The site has no saved guild chest logs. This batch's {count} new rows will be the first saved records. If the historical log is incomplete, confirm an inventory baseline before applying.
adminShopImport.stagingNoNewBody: The site's last applied log {when}{tail} is included in this batch and there are no new rows. There is nothing to apply.
adminShopImport.stagingSkippedBody: This batch doesn't overlap the site's last applied log {when}{tail} and has no new rows. The pasted range may already be an applied past section.
adminShopImport.stagingBackfillBody: There are no new rows after the site's latest record {when}{tail}, but this older pasted range contains {count} saveable rows. Confirm this is an intentional missing-range backfill.
adminShopImport.stagingContinuedTitle: New entries detected after the last log
adminShopImport.stagingContinuedBody: {count} new rows were detected after the site's last applied log {when}{tail}. Ready to apply to stock.
adminShopImport.stagingGapDangerTitle: Log gap of {gap} detected (likely missing entries)
adminShopImport.stagingGapDangerBody: No logs for {gap} after the site's last applied log {when}{tail} in this batch. You likely missed a chunk before the in-game log rolled over — consider a baseline reset.
adminShopImport.stagingGapWarnBody: No logs for {gap} after the site's last applied log {when}{tail} in this batch. If transactions happened in the gap, stock will be out of sync with reality.
adminShopImport.stagingGapNoOverlapTitle: No overlap with the last log (may be missing entries)
adminShopImport.stagingGapNoOverlapBody: No row in this batch overlaps the site's last applied log {when}{tail}.{gapSuffix} Some logs in between may be missing.
adminShopImport.unresolvedHint: Couldn't match the Korean name in the bundle dictionary. Blacklist it if it's junk.
adminShopImport.stockPreviewTitle: Expected stock changes · applied when confirmed ({count})
adminShopImport.commitPriceSyncDeferred: Stock is updated. Price refresh now runs separately via the equipment price refresh button above or the automatic sync.

adminShopImportFilter.title: Import tier filter
adminShopImportFilter.description: Exclude new chest-log rows before saving/stock updates by item tier + log enchant. Example: Elder's Mace enchant 2 = 8 + 2 = 10.
adminShopImportFilter.lteHint: Exclude logs whose sum is at or below this value.
adminShopImportFilter.gteHint: Exclude logs whose sum is at or above this value.
adminShopImportFilter.rangeHint: Integer {min}~{max}; leave blank to disable that condition
adminShopImportFilter.previewDisabled: All tier/enchant logs are currently applied.
adminShopImportFilter.previewBoth: Exclude {lte} or below and {gte} or above
adminShopImportFilter.invalidRange: Enter an integer from 0 to 12, or leave it blank.
adminShopImportFilter.invalidWindow: When both values are set, the lower cutoff must be less than the upper cutoff.

regearBreakdown.manualEditDescription: Update the silver amount you're claiming. The cap for your role is {cap}s.
regearBreakdown.overchargeEditDescription: Update the amount claimed for gear destroyed by overcharge. The cap for your role is {cap}s.

regearBuildSnapshot.title: Craft build info

adminAllowUnverified.title: Allow unverified members to access the site
adminAllowUnverified.description: Default is off. When off, members who haven't completed Albion verification are redirected to the onboarding page on site entry and can't use any other page until verified. Admins, guest invite links, and public paths are always exempt.
adminAllowUnverified.toggleLabel: Let unverified members use the site
adminAllowUnverified.toggleHint: When off, site access is blocked until onboarding is complete.

adminTimezone.title: Guild timezone
adminTimezone.description: Event gather times, leaderboard/streak day boundaries, and Discord notification timestamps are all rendered in this timezone.
adminTimezone.hint: Changes take effect on the next server-rendered page load. Invalid values silently fall back to Korea (KST).

adminCdBadge.title: CD badge role filter
adminCdBadge.descriptionLine1: Pick which roles show the weapon skill cooldown badge (including leather armor / food reductions).
adminCdBadge.descriptionLine2: Defaults to Engage DPS only — check other roles if needed. If nothing is selected, no slot shows the badge.

adminShopSilverRate.title: Shop exchange / discount rate
adminShopSilverRate.description:
Enter the rate (%) applied to silver prices.
• 100 → 1:1 (1M silver → 1,000,000p)
• 50 → half price (1M silver → 500,000p)
• 30 → 30% of silver price (1M silver → 300,000p)
Applies to both manual prices and automatic (market silver) prices.

adminAodp.title: Market price settings
adminAodp.description: Shared price-lookup options used by shop auto-pricing and auto regear.
adminAodp.cityHint: Pick one city as your guild's home market. We use this city's price first, fall back to a pooled median across the other royal cities when it has no data (closest to the in-game estimate), and only widen to the red zone if still nothing found.
adminAodp.modeAvg14dHint: Long-term average · cushions sudden price swings
adminAodp.qualityHint: If a dropped item's quality is below this value, the lookup uses this quality instead. Default 1 (no adjustment).

adminAlbionHomeGuild.title: Home guild · Albion server
adminAlbionHomeGuild.description: Sets the server and "our guild" used for Albion onboarding and killboard auto-verification. Guild IDs differ per server, so the two values are always saved as a pair. If the home guild is empty, all onboardings are saved as [unverified].
adminAlbionHomeGuild.unsetWarning: Unset — saving now will mark all onboardings as [unverified]
adminAlbionHomeGuild.firstTimeWarningTitle: Warning — once saved, this can't be changed
adminAlbionHomeGuild.firstTimeWarningBody: The home guild anchors member verification, killboard, and regear data. After the first save, regular admins can no longer change it. If the wrong guild is registered, ask the site operator to unlock it.
adminAlbionHomeGuild.lockedBody: This site's home guild is already set and can't be changed. If the wrong guild is registered, ask the site operator to unlock it.
adminAlbionHomeGuild.superAdminHint: You're bypassing the lock with super admin privileges. Changing the guild will re-evaluate member verification, killboards, and regear against the new guild.

adminRegearLimits.title: Regear submission limits
adminRegearLimits.description: Set how long members must wait before regear requests open, how many death regear claims one person can file per event, and when new submissions expire. Overcharge claims do not count as deaths.
adminRegearLimits.windowMinutesHint: {min}–{max} minutes. Members can file regear requests once this many minutes pass after the battle starts, or as soon as the battle ends — whichever comes first. The buffer gives Albion's killboard time to index death records on long battles.
adminRegearLimits.maxDeathsHint: {min}–{max}. The maximum number of death regear claims one member can file for the same event. Overcharge claims do not count, and rejected requests don't count so members can retry.
adminRegearLimits.eligibilityDaysHint: {min}–{max} days. Event regear and tracked deaths older than this can no longer be newly submitted and disappear from the "eligible regear" list. Already-submitted requests are not affected.

adminEventAutoStart.title: Auto-start events
adminEventAutoStart.description: The site automatically marks an event as 'Battle Started' once its gather time has passed. Regear requests then open at the scheduled time without an admin having to press Start.
adminEventAutoStart.enabledHint: When enabled, the site checks every 5 minutes and auto-starts any event whose gather time has passed. Only events within the last 30 minutes are processed to avoid bulk-starting old events.

adminRegearPayoutRate.title: Regear payout and cap policy
adminRegearPayoutRate.description: Set how much of a regear claim is paid out in silver. Requests with video proof can use a separate payout rate and claim ceiling. Payout rates apply to future approvals; claim caps apply to new submissions and edits.
adminRegearPayoutRate.percentHint: {min}–{max}%. For example, at 80%, approving a 10,000-silver claim pays out 8,000 silver.
adminRegearPayoutRate.videoPercentHint: {min}–{max}%. Requests with a YouTube video use this rate instead of the base rate.
adminRegearPayoutRate.videoClaimCeilingBonusSilverHint: Enter an integer of {min} or higher. Requests with a video can claim the base role cap plus this silver amount.

adminAutoRegearSlots.title: Auto-regear included slots
adminAutoRegearSlots.descriptionLine1: Choose which slots auto-regear sums when estimating market price. Unchecked slots are excluded from estimated/payout amounts.
adminAutoRegearSlots.descriptionLine2: Example: unchecking food/potion/mount limits the claim to weapon and armor. Manual regear and matching rules are unaffected.

publicDocsHome.title: Start with the decisions a new guild actually needs.
publicDocsHome.lead: AGM connects Discord bot install, guild address setup, Albion character verification, first event publishing, and post-fight regear claims into one operations flow.
publicDocsHome.memberPromise: This is not only an admin tool. Members should be able to sign up, verify themselves, and check rewards without asking an officer. This minimum guide covers the path to that first success.
publicDocsHome.quickStartLead: Complete these steps and members can enter the site, link their character, and sign up for the first event.
publicDocsHome.quickStartStep1: Invite the bot with a Discord account that has Manage Server permission.
publicDocsHome.quickStartStep2: Use the setup wizard to save the guild URL, Albion home guild, timezone, and active member roles.
publicDocsHome.quickStartStep3: Connect the event announcement channel and send a test post to verify the Discord path.
publicDocsHome.quickStartStep4: Publish the first event, then share the invite link so members finish Discord login and Albion character verification.
publicDocsHome.minimumSetLead: If you understand permissions, member verification, the first event, and regear rules, you can decide whether to start operating with AGM.

publicDocsHome.memberVerificationBody: Members log in with Discord and connect an Albion character name. When it matches the home guild, their events, regear, and stats attach to their own record.
publicDocsHome.firstEventBody: Officers create an event, fill slots or a build sheet, then send a Discord announcement. Members use the link to sign up and check attendance status.
publicDocsHome.regearRulesBody: Auto regear creates claims awaiting review from black-zone deaths and battle aggregation rules. Claimants can review prices, then admins approve payout.

publicFeatures.pageSubtitle: Automate the core guild workflow first
publicFeatures.pageLead: Clean ZvZ analytics, event/build signup, and member self-service come first. Regear, shop, and craft tools are review-based automation layered on top.
publicFeatures.f1Body: Build parties and slots, publish, and the bot pushes an @everyone alert to your channel. Members sign up for slots on the web and check in for attendance.
publicFeatures.f2Body: Killboard syncs every 5 minutes to find candidate deaths, then AODP market data prepares a draft claim. Final payout is confirmed only after claimant review and admin approval.
publicFeatures.f2Bullet1: 5-minute killboard candidates + AODP pricing from your primary city
publicFeatures.f2Bullet2: Per-slot price edit, re-issue, reject workflow
publicFeatures.f2Bullet3: Blackzone-only · claimant review + admin approval (two-stage) · global off toggle
publicFeatures.f3Body: Run an internal shop where regear / event points buy in-game items. Exchange rate equals discount — silver and points are 1:1, so the math stays intuitive.
publicFeatures.f4Title: ZvZ Analytics — discover your members' true specialties
publicFeatures.f4Body: Other Albion tools just dump raw killboards. We extract real ZvZ only — auto-filtering ganks and low-engagement fights, counting only records after a member joins. The result: per-member weapon-category specialty, matchup-by-matchup guild records, attendance, and survival rate.
publicFeatures.f4Bullet1: Matchup-level guild records — N–M against this guild
publicFeatures.f4Bullet2: Per-member weapon category specialty + K/D + survival rate
publicFeatures.f5Body: When the guild enables crafted regear, new claims are created as craft candidates. Admins finish each claim during review as silver payout, craft-queue task, or stock issue; crafters then build the gear and deliver it to pickup boxes.
publicFeatures.f5Bullet2: Review-time choice: silver payout / craft queue / stock issue
publicFeatures.f6Title: Build-sheet recruitment — reusable ZvZ gear in one click
publicFeatures.f6Body: Large ZvZ events repeat the same locus, tank, and Engage DPS builds over and over. Officers prepare build sheets once, then apply them from an image-first palette inside the event editor.
publicFeatures.f6Bullet1: Save build sheets by role and category
publicFeatures.f6Bullet2: Pick from gear-image cards instead of text-only rows
publicFeatures.f6Bullet3: Slot, build-sheet, and hybrid recruitment modes

publicSeoFeatures.discordBotHeading: Albion guild Discord bot with a full operations dashboard.
publicSeoFeatures.discordBotLead: Start from Discord OAuth, invite the bot, connect roles and channels, then let members move from announcements into the right web flow.
publicSeoFeatures.discordBotProblem: Guilds often split operations across Discord posts, spreadsheets, and one-off bots. Officers answer the same setup and attendance questions repeatedly.
publicSeoFeatures.discordBotOutcome: One bot becomes the entry point for setup, announcements, event signup, permissions, and member self-service.
publicSeoFeatures.discordBotStep1: Invite the bot from the canonical site with Manage Server permission.
publicSeoFeatures.discordBotStep2: Choose the admin role, active-member role, announcement channel, and Albion home guild.
publicSeoFeatures.discordBotStep3: Members open Discord links and land on the correct guild page, event, or personal dashboard.
publicSeoFeatures.discordBotProof2: Announcement links that lead into event and member flows.
publicSeoFeatures.discordBotProof3: Self-serve onboarding for newly invited guilds.
publicSeoFeatures.discordBotFaqQuestion: Does the bot need broad Discord permissions?
publicSeoFeatures.discordBotFaqAnswer: No. It uses the guild setup and messaging permissions needed for the workflow, while admin access is still controlled by configured Discord roles.
publicSeoFeatures.autoRegearMetaTitle: Albion Auto Regear for ZvZ Guilds | AlbionGuildManager
publicSeoFeatures.autoRegearMetaDescription: Automate Albion Online regear claims with killboard sync, black-zone filtering, market pricing, claimant review, and admin approval.
publicSeoFeatures.autoRegearHeading: Albion auto regear that starts from real ZvZ deaths.
publicSeoFeatures.autoRegearLead: Killboard data, price estimates, claimant review, and admin approval stay in one workflow instead of a spreadsheet.
publicSeoFeatures.autoRegearProblem: After a fight, officers manually search deaths, estimate item values, ask members for corrections, and track payouts in scattered notes.
publicSeoFeatures.autoRegearOutcome: Eligible black-zone deaths become pending claims, members can review item prices, and admins finish the payout or craft decision from one queue.
publicSeoFeatures.autoRegearStep1: Sync Albion kill records and match deaths to verified guild members.
publicSeoFeatures.autoRegearStep2: Create pending claims with editable per-slot prices and recheck controls.
publicSeoFeatures.autoRegearStep3: Approve as silver payout, craft task, stock issue, or rejection based on guild policy.
publicSeoFeatures.autoRegearProof3: Silver, crafted regear, and stock-issue finish paths.
publicSeoFeatures.autoRegearFaqQuestion: Will every death become an automatic regear claim?
publicSeoFeatures.autoRegearFaqAnswer: No. Automatic regear is limited to black-zone eligible deaths and still goes through claimant review and admin approval.
publicSeoFeatures.zvzKillboardMetaTitle: Albion ZvZ Killboard and Battle Tracker | AlbionGuildManager
publicSeoFeatures.zvzKillboardMetaDescription: Track Albion Online ZvZ battles with killboard sync, gank filtering, matchup records, member stats, and weapon-category analysis.
publicSeoFeatures.zvzKillboardHeading: Albion ZvZ killboard data cleaned for guild decisions.
publicSeoFeatures.zvzKillboardLead: Raw killboards are noisy. AlbionGuildManager filters low-value fights and rolls real ZvZ battles into records officers can act on.
publicSeoFeatures.zvzKillboardProblem: Generic killboard views mix ganks, low-engagement fights, old records, and unrelated player activity with the battles officers need to evaluate.
publicSeoFeatures.zvzKillboardOutcome: Guild battles, matchup history, member performance, and weapon-category tendencies share the same cleaned ZvZ standard.
publicSeoFeatures.zvzKillboardStep1: Sync official Albion kill data on a schedule.
publicSeoFeatures.zvzKillboardStep2: Bundle records into battles and exclude small ganks or low-engagement noise.
publicSeoFeatures.zvzKillboardStep3: Roll results into member stats, matchup records, and leaderboards.
publicSeoFeatures.zvzKillboardProof1: Battle-level records instead of raw kill dumps.
publicSeoFeatures.zvzKillboardProof2: Weapon category aggregation for real role tendencies.
publicSeoFeatures.zvzKillboardProof3: Shared rules for battles, achievements, and stats.
publicSeoFeatures.zvzKillboardFaqQuestion: Why not show every kill exactly as the Albion feed returns it?
publicSeoFeatures.zvzKillboardFaqAnswer: The raw feed is preserved where needed, but operations stats use cleaned battle rules so ganks and low-engagement fights do not distort guild decisions.
publicSeoFeatures.guildEventsMetaTitle: Albion Guild Event Signup and Build Sheets | AlbionGuildManager
publicSeoFeatures.guildEventsMetaDescription: Run Albion Online guild events with slot signup, build sheets, Discord announcements, attendance, tentative roles, and post-fight follow-up.
publicSeoFeatures.guildEventsHeading: Albion guild event signup with reusable ZvZ build sheets.
publicSeoFeatures.guildEventsLead: Create the event, fill role slots from saved builds, publish to Discord, and keep attendance connected to rewards.
publicSeoFeatures.guildEventsProblem: ZvZ rosters are rebuilt repeatedly in Discord messages, while members lose track of slot state, tentative roles, and event follow-up.
publicSeoFeatures.guildEventsOutcome: Published events connect signup, build sheets, attendance, and regear follow-up under one event link.

publicSeoFeatures.guildEventsStep2: Publish the event and send Discord announcements to the configured channel.
publicSeoFeatures.guildEventsStep3: Members sign up, update tentative roles, and return for attendance or follow-up.
publicSeoFeatures.guildEventsProof1: Slot, build-sheet, and hybrid recruitment modes.
publicSeoFeatures.guildEventsProof3: Attendance context reused by rewards and records.

publicSeoFeatures.guildEventsFaqAnswer: Yes. Build sheets let officers save repeated gear patterns and apply them through image-first cards in the event editor.
publicSeoFeatures.guildShopMetaTitle: Albion Guild Shop and Points Exchange | AlbionGuildManager
publicSeoFeatures.guildShopMetaDescription: Run an Albion guild shop with point exchange, inventory baselines, restock tracking, payout approval, and exchange-rate controls.
publicSeoFeatures.guildShopHeading: Albion guild shop with point exchange and inventory control.
publicSeoFeatures.guildShopLead: Turn guild points into a controlled internal shop while keeping stock, rates, and payout requests visible to officers.
publicSeoFeatures.guildShopProblem: Guild banks and point exchanges become hard to audit when stock, discounts, member requests, and payouts live in separate spreadsheets.
publicSeoFeatures.guildShopOutcome: Members shop with points, officers approve exchanges, and stock movement stays tied to baselines and variance reports.
publicSeoFeatures.guildShopStep1: Register inventory and preserve a baseline for stock replay.
publicSeoFeatures.guildShopStep2: Set the exchange rate that also acts as the discount rate.
publicSeoFeatures.guildShopStep3: Approve orders, exchange requests, payouts, and stock corrections from admin screens.
publicSeoFeatures.guildShopProof2: Exchange rate equals discount rate for simple math.
publicSeoFeatures.guildShopProof3: Baseline, restock, withdrawal, and variance tracking.
publicSeoFeatures.guildShopFaqQuestion: Why is exchange rate the same as discount rate?
publicSeoFeatures.guildShopFaqAnswer: A 100% rate means one point equals one silver, while 50% means items sell for half the silver price in points. The single value keeps guild policy understandable.

publicSeoFeatures.guildStatsStep2: Aggregate weapon categories, attendance, survival, and achievement signals.

publicSeoFeatures.guildStatsProof1: Per-member K/D, attendance, and survival views.

publicFaq.pageLead: Before installing, here are the questions guild leaders usually ask about permissions, data, pricing, and auto-regear rules.
publicFaq.q1: What Discord permissions does the bot need?
publicFaq.a1: Anyone with Manage Server permission can install. The bot uses only message-send, member-read, and role-read scopes.
publicFaq.q2: How does it pull Albion guild data?
publicFaq.a2: We pull Albion's official data every 5 minutes to refresh kill records. Loss values come from AODP (Albion Online Data Project) — a public dataset where players share market prices they collect in-game.
publicFaq.a4: In a secure cloud database. Guilds are isolated — no other guild can read your data. When a guild is deleted, the data isn't wiped immediately; it's retained for a period and then cleaned up.
publicFaq.a5: All official servers — Americas, Europe, and Asia. Pick your server during onboarding and the bot uses that server's kill records and price data.
publicFaq.q6: Can I delegate admin to other members?
publicFaq.a6: Yes. Admin is granted by Discord role: anyone with the configured admin role is automatically an admin on the site.
publicFaq.a7: One Discord server = one guild site for now. Multi-guild management is planned for a future release.
publicFaq.q8: What happens if my guild stops using it?
publicFaq.a8: Guilds with no admin login for 30+ days are flagged inactive. After further inactivity we may suspend with notice (data preserved).
publicFaq.a9: The default sign-in is Discord OAuth. If a guild enables Albion account entry, only a hash of the site-only password is stored; we never ask for Discord passwords or Albion game credentials. All traffic is encrypted, and data is isolated per guild.
publicFaq.q10: How do I fully delete my guild from the site?
publicFaq.a10: Admins can request deletion from inside the site. Data is retained for 30 days, then permanently erased. You can recover during that window; after permanent deletion, member stats, event history, and kill records are gone.
publicFaq.q11: How is this different from other Albion tools (Battle Tabs, standalone Discord bots, etc.)?
publicFaq.a11: Event ops (party building, DM reminders, attendance points), reward automation (auto regear, guild shop, point exchange), and ZvZ stats are unified in one site, so you don't need spreadsheets or multiple Discord bots. We pull from Discord and the Albion kill records directly, so manual input is minimal.
publicFaq.q12: Aren't the bot's permissions too broad?
publicFaq.a12: The bot uses only message-send, member/role read, and DM-send. It doesn't read message content or touch voice channels. If permissions feel too broad, an admin can further constrain the bot role directly from Discord server settings.
publicFaq.q13: What should I do first after installing the bot?
publicFaq.a13: 1) Sign in with Discord after inviting the bot, 2) set your guild's address, 3) pick your Albion home guild, 4) assign the event-announcement channel and the active-member role, 5) review operating policies like auto-regear and the guild shop — once these five are done, members can sign in and link their Albion characters.
publicFaq.q14: What does a member do the first time they visit the site?
publicFaq.a14: Signing in with Discord starts the verification flow automatically. Enter your Albion character name to match the guild roster — once verified, your kill log, claims, and reward points start accumulating automatically. Entering a character that isn't on the guild roster leaves you in [unverified] state and some features will be limited.
publicFaq.q15: My death isn't getting picked up by auto-regear. Why?
publicFaq.a15: 1) Albion's kill records take about 30 minutes to appear in the official feed after a death — wait a moment and press 'Recheck' on the regear page. 2) Auto-regear only catches deaths in the black zone. Yellow/red-zone or non-ZvZ deaths must be submitted manually. 3) Make sure your Albion character is verified and that your guild matches the site's home guild.
publicFaq.q16: How do I customize my guild’s public page?
publicFaq.a16: Admins can edit the `/g/your-guild` page directly — banner image, banner opacity, accent color, description, recruitment status, Discord invite link, active hours, and supported languages. You can also toggle individual sections on or off (member count, battle records, weapon mix, rival guilds, admin team, and more). Use the "Edit banner" button at the top of the public page, or open the public profile settings in the admin panel.
publicFaq.q17: Which languages does the site support?
publicFaq.a17: The site UI ships in Korean, Japanese, English, and Simplified Chinese. Switch language from the top-right language menu and every page updates immediately. Note that the documentation pages (`/docs`) themselves are currently Korean-only; translations are in progress.
publicFaq.q18: The public page shows the Albion English guild name. Can I show our Discord name instead?
publicFaq.a18: The public page (`/g/your-guild`) and SEO metadata always prefer your in-game Albion guild name (English) — Albion only permits English characters in guild names, and matching that name keeps the page consistent with how other players search for you or track you on the killboard. The localized Discord name is only used inside admin surfaces. To change your home guild after first setup, contact the operator (super-admin).
publicFaq.ctaTitle: Still unsure? Start with the demo.
publicFaq.ctaBody: Read the docs to understand the rules, then use the demo to see how member and admin screens connect.

battleTracking.tipMatch: This view preserves Albion battle originals as a ledger and renders a separate guild-facing observation view.
battleTracking.tipEngagement: Only ZvZ battles your guild directly joined appear in the default tab. Ganking, small-scale, and low-engagement records keep their source data and stay visible in the excluded tab.
battleTracking.tipOutcome: Results are shown as advantage, disadvantage, even, or unclear from kill fame instead of hard win/loss claims.
battleTracking.tipLimitation: When the old aggregation and the ledger projection disagree, the battle remains in the review tab for inspection.
battleTracking.rulesIntro: This page does not delete source battles. It separates them by observation scope and activity classification. Stats, achievements, and killbot battle summaries use direct battles classified as ZvZ by default.
battleTracking.rule1Body: Direct means your guild appears in the battle original. Alliance means your guild is absent, but a guild in the same alliance at battle time appears.
battleTracking.rule2Intro: Decided by whichever is larger between home and the main opponent (the largest single alliance or standalone guild).
battleTracking.rule2CutOff: Anything under 10 is treated as ganking/stragglers and excluded. The Albion Disarray threshold, 21 players, is the start of ZvZ candidacy; 18–20 player groups remain ganking/small-scale/review candidates.
battleTracking.rule3Body: The default tab shows only ZvZ: both forces at 21+ players with mutual engagement or sustained duration. One-sided 20-player catches, ganking-event windows, and low-engagement records are excluded from default stats.
battleTracking.rule3Why: Why? To keep 20-player ganks and drive-by participation from inflating win rate, achievements, and killbot battle summaries. Source data is retained in the excluded tab with admin overrides.
battleTracking.rule4Body: Advantage/disadvantage is shown only when a single direct engagement has enough evidence. When multiple battles or forces are grouped from battle-summary evidence, the result stays unclear because Albion logs can merge unrelated ongoing fights.
battleTracking.rule5Body: If you engaged two or more opposing alliances/standalone guilds in the same battle, the matchups are split into separate rows ("1/2" badge + same-battle marker). We do not collapse them into one row so you can see who fought whom and how.
battleTracking.rule6Body: Newly detected battles are flagged "Pending" until killboard data settles, then resolved automatically.
battleTracking.rulesLimit1: Side approximation — in a free-for-all where multiple standalone guilds (no alliance) fight individually, the opponent side may be over-aggregated (everyone outside home is treated as one side).
battleTracking.rulesLimit2: Only battles exposed via Albion's public API are tracked. Private skirmishes (small non-ZvZ ganks, etc.) are not aggregated.
battleTracking.listDescription: Albion battle originals are interpreted from your guild's point of view. Review direct, alliance-only, excluded, and diff records separately.
battleTracking.pausedBody: Battle records, killboard sync, killbot, and the public battle board are paused while the UI/UX refresh is in progress.
battleTracking.pausedDetail: Existing data is preserved. New battlelog collection and backfills will not run until the feature resumes.

shop.aodpTooltip: Market prices come from AODP (Albion Online Data Project) — a public dataset where players share market prices they capture from the game. Data density varies by server, city, and time, so when recent prices aren't available for the configured base city, the system falls back through lower quality → 14-day average → other royal cities → red-zone cities. When that fallback chain runs, the estimate may diverge from real trade value, and a "Price estimate" warning is shown.

priceWarningBuyer.quality: Price estimate: no market data for this item quality, so we substituted a lower-quality price.
priceWarningBuyer.window: Price estimate: recent market data is sparse, averaged over up to 14 days.
priceWarningBuyer.bluezone: Price estimate: no price data for the current city, so we used another Royal City's price. Actual trades may incur teleport cost and travel time.
priceWarningBuyer.redzone: Price estimate: no Royal City data at all — we used Red Zone prices (Caerleon / Brecilien). Actual value may differ significantly due to PvP risk.

priceWarningAdmin.quality: Price estimate: no data for the requested quality, so we substituted a lower-quality price.
priceWarningAdmin.window: Price estimate: recent market data is sparse, averaged over up to 14 days.
priceWarningAdmin.bluezone: Price estimate: no data for the configured city, so we used another Royal City's price.
priceWarningAdmin.redzone: Price estimate: no Royal City data at all — using Red Zone prices. Actual value may differ significantly; admin review recommended.

home.introBody: Review the public profile, admin queue, member dashboard, battle tracking, and weapon analytics flow.
home.step1Body: Recruitment status, alliance and timezone surfaced instantly. The same page used for Discord shares and SEO indexing.
home.step2Body: Regear, exchange, point top-up, shop, payout, and craft requests collected into one card. No more channel hopping.
home.step3Body: Once Discord + Albion are linked, members see their own K/D, attendance, and regear history in one view. No more payout disputes.
home.step4Body: Events, wins/losses, and K/D refresh automatically. Guild trends visible without spreadsheets.
home.step5Body: Only the ZvZ battles your guild joined are auto-classified, with K/D and matchup labelled automatically. No need to dig through the killboard.
home.step6Body: Weapon category distribution gives evidence-based build decisions.
home.completedBody: Now explore Events, Members, Settings and Backup from the sidebar.

events.introBody: Walk through the same order as the real admin home: required setup, today's work, invite link, and event list.
events.step1Body: Confirm the items needed before operations, such as announcement channels, home guild, and public profile settings.
events.step2Body: Pending approvals, required setup, sync health, and member verification are summarized as cards.
events.step3Body: Copy the URL new guild members use to start Discord login and Albion verification.
events.step4Body: This is the entry point for creating and publishing upcoming ZvZ events for guild-wide announcements.
events.step5Body: Recurring meetups become templates once, then seed the next event when needed.
events.step6Body: Each event card manages participants, weapon/gear slot assignments, and the schedule in one place.
events.completedBody: The demo now follows the real operations home from today's work through event publishing.

builds.introBody: See how reusable ZvZ gear builds are saved and then loaded from the event editor palette.
builds.step1Body: Officers create new builds and search existing builds from here.
builds.step2Body: Find similar gear sets by role or build name before editing an event.
builds.step3Body: Weapon and armor icons make similar builds easier to distinguish than text-only rows.
builds.completedBody: In the real event editor, these build cards feed directly into the slot palette.

regear.introBody: Walk through the unified queue for regear, exchanges, point top-ups, shop orders, payouts, and craft work.
regear.step1Body: Regear, exchange, point top-up, shop order, payout, craft — every admin approval funneled into one page. Badges show pending counts.
regear.step2Body: Auto regear is generated by cron from the killboard; manual is filed by members. Filter them separately to review.
regear.step3Body: Each regear card lets you adjust per-slot prices (head/chest/hands/feet/weapon/shield/mount). Claimants tune to current market.
regear.completedBody: Other approval type tabs (exchange/point top-up/shop) follow the same flow.

members.introBody: Review member status, tab grouping, and member detail navigation.
members.step1Body: Total members + this week's cumulative participation appear directly in the header.
members.step2Body: Members · Roster · Guests · Withdrawn — four tabs separate full members, the roster list, temporary guests, and leavers.
members.completedBody: Click any member row for personal stats and regear history.

stats.introBody: See how point balances, holders, finance flow, and operating metrics are presented.
stats.step1Body: Total held points, lifetime earned/spent, holder count — four KPI cards capture your guild's economy at a glance.

stats.step3Body: Daily earned/spent chart for the last N days + breakdown by source and sink. Track where points come in and go out.
stats.completedBody: Scroll further for verification, event participation, shop & regear stats.

audit.introBody: Track who changed what when disputes or mistakes need review.

audit.step3Body: Paginated 10 entries per page by default. Total count is always visible at the top.
audit.completedBody: Try changing the filters — picture how you'd use this for disputes inside your own guild.

events.title: Events start here

eventDetail.title: Use the detail page to claim a slot

exchange.title: Exchange requests live in My info

publicPricing.title: Every feature is free until general availability.
publicPricing.subtitle: This phase is about proving that guild leaders save time and members actually enjoy using the app. Invite the Discord bot and start without a payment setup.
publicPricing.planBody: Events, regear, shop, crafting, stats, and public guild pages are available without feature caps during beta.
publicPricing.includedEvents: Event creation, publishing, slot signup, Discord alerts
publicPricing.includedStats: Killboard sync, battle aggregation, member stats, leaderboard
publicPricing.includedRegear: Automatic and manual regear claims with approval flow
publicPricing.includedShop: Guild shop, point exchange, stock variance tracking
publicPricing.includedCraft: Craft regear queue, crafter tasks, pickup box flow
publicPricing.includedPublicProfile: Public guild page, recruitment info, public battle profile
publicPricing.betaPolicyBody: During beta we do not ask for cards or in-game currency payments. Discord login and bot invite are enough to start.
publicPricing.futurePolicyTitle: Paid plans will be announced first
publicPricing.futurePolicyBody: If paid plans are introduced, existing guilds will get at least 30 days of notice plus clear options to keep using the service, export data, or migrate.
publicPricing.supportPolicyBody: The key question is whether it works for real guild operations. Send feature requests and bug reports through the official Discord.
publicPricing.validationTitle: Before paying for anything, test the real guild workflow.
publicPricing.validationLead: The free period is not just a trial. It is time to see whether AGM fits your guild's operating style: publish one event, let members sign up, then watch how records and rewards connect after the fight.
publicPricing.validationEventsBody: Check whether publishing events and collecting slot signups actually saves officer time.
publicPricing.validationMembersBody: See whether members can find their wallet, regear, siphon, and rankings without help.
publicPricing.validationDataBody: Review whether killboard sync, battle aggregation, and leaderboards match your guild's ZvZ standards.
publicPricing.questionTitle: Want to check more before installing?
publicPricing.questionBody: Use the demo to see the full flow, then read the docs to understand the intent and operating model before inviting the bot.

publicLegal.privacyIntro: AlbionGuildManager processes only the account, guild, and game-operations data needed to run the service. We do not ask for Albion game passwords or payment information.
publicLegal.privacyDataBody: We store Discord user IDs, display names, avatars, server and role data, Albion character names, guild IDs, event signups, regear claims, shop/points/siphon/craft records, and other data needed for guild operations.
publicLegal.privacyUseBody: We use the data for login, guild-scoped permission checks, event operations, killboard and battle analytics, reward processing, guild shop, craft regear, and audit logs.
publicLegal.privacySharingBody: Guild data is isolated by guild and cannot be viewed by other guilds. Only the fields that a guild admin enables for the public guild page are publicly visible.
publicLegal.privacyRetentionBody: After a guild deletion request, data goes through a recoverable retention period before cleanup. Minimal records may be kept when required for legal obligations or security investigation.
publicLegal.privacyCredentialsBody: We do not collect Albion game passwords, Discord passwords, payment cards, or government identity documents. Default sign-in uses Discord OAuth; optional guild-local Albion account entry stores only a hash of the site-only password.
publicLegal.termsIntro: These terms describe the basic conditions for using the AlbionGuildManager beta. Guild admins are responsible for explaining the service purpose and data use to their members.
publicLegal.termsBetaBody: The service is currently in beta, and features, screens, and policies may change. Any future paid plan will be announced in advance.
publicLegal.termsAdminBody: Guild admins manage Discord roles, site permissions, public-page visibility, and reward policies. Internal disputes caused by incorrect permissions or operational input should be handled by the guild leadership first.
publicLegal.termsGameDataBody: Killboard, market, and battle data are calculated from external public data and guild input, so delays or inaccuracies may occur. Final reward approval and payout remain the guild admin’s responsibility.
publicLegal.termsFairUseBody: Access may be limited if the service is used to scrape other guilds, spam bot notifications, or attempt security bypasses.
publicLegal.termsAvailabilityBody: We work to keep the service stable, but external systems such as Albion official APIs, Discord, Supabase, and Vercel can cause temporary delays or outages.
publicLegal.termsChangesBody: Terms and policies may be updated as the service evolves. Questions and reports are handled through the official Discord channel.
